title: The optimal randomized metric distortion in social choice
area: Algorithmic game theory, mechanism design and fair division
formal: Determine the infimum universal constant D for which an ordinal voting rule always selects a lottery whose expected total metric cost is at most D times the optimal candidate cost, over all numbers of voters and candidates and all consistent metrics.
context:
Use unrestricted randomized ordinal rules; the old conjecture D=2 is false, and tournament-only rules are a different restricted model.

This short research proposal states the target identified in the September 2026 fundamental-problem search. The references give the source models and related results. A full self-contained formulation and detailed progress review remain to be written.
why: A defining limit on how much welfare can be recovered from ordinal preferences.

sentences: Metric distortion measures the welfare loss caused by choosing among candidates using only voters' rankings rather than their distances.
The proposal asks for the optimal universal factor achieved by a randomized voting rule.
The same ranking profile can be consistent with several metrics having very different total candidate costs.
A sharp factor would quantify the unavoidable price of missing cardinal preference information.
The objective is expected total metric cost, and the saved proposal still needs full conventions for consistent metrics, ties, and the class of ordinal rules before becoming a finished card.
